turns.question: How do errors propagate through the middleware composition path?
turns.text:
<ghx-report>
{
  "answer": "Errors propagate via two nested try/catch layers plus a customizable handler chain. Inside compose.ts's dispatch(i), each middleware/handler call is wrapped in try/catch (compose.ts lines ~47-57): if it throws an Error and an onError was supplied, dispatch calls onError(err,context), sets context.error, and treats it as a handled response (isError=true); otherwise it rethrows. At the top level, hono-base.ts's #dispatch (lines 407-464) wraps the composed(c) call in try/catch and forwards any escaping error to #handleError (line 400), which calls this.errorHandler(err,c) if err is an Error (otherwise rethrows uncaught). The default errorHandler (lines 35-42) special-cases HTTPException-like errors (objects with getResponse()) into their Response, else logs and returns a generic 500; app.onError() (line 272) lets users override this.errorHandler. For sub-apps mounted with app.route() (lines 219-227), if the sub-app has a non-default errorHandler, its routes are wrapped with compose([], app.errorHandler) so the sub-app's own error handler catches errors locally before they could bubble to the parent's handler.",

Inside compose.ts's dispatch(i), each middleware/handler call is wrapped in try/catch (compose.ts lines ~47-57): if it throws an Error and an onError was supplied, dispatch calls onError(err,context), sets context.error, and treats it as a handled response (isError=true); otherwise it rethrows. For sub-apps mounted with app.route() (lines 219-227), if the sub-app has a non-default errorHandler, its routes are wrapped with compose([], app.errorHandler) so the sub-app's own error handler catches errors locally before they could bubble to the parent's handler.
